ashby:aerovect:d05135a5-2796-4c68-b4a5-f.summary:
AeroVect is transforming ground handling with autonomy, redefining how airlines and ground service providers around the globe run day-to-day operations. We are a Series A company backed by top-tier venture capital investors in aviation and autonomous driving. Our customers include some of the world’s largest airlines and ground handling providers. For more information, visit www.aerovect.com .

The Sr. PMT for Fleet Operations is responsible for defining the strategy, roadmap, and development of products that enable AeroVect’s Autonomous Ground Support Equipment (AGSE) vehicles to operate safely and reliably at scale. This role will define and build the remote assistance infrastructure, dispatch systems, and fleet monitoring tooling that the AeroVect AGSE Service depends on to scale reliably.

sections.title: Who We Are
paras: This role requires a unique blend of user-centric product thinking, technical fluency, and strong communication skills to drive the creation of reliable and scalable fleet operations products. The PMT will translate the real-world needs of airline/airport customers and internal operators into a clear, prioritized product roadmap. The PMT is expected to decompose user needs into high-level system design and clear requirements that engineering teams can execute against. Delivery against the roadmap will require strong cross-functional collaboration with UX, infrastructure, autonomy, and operations teams to ensure that products are intuitive and reliable.

sections.title: You Will
bullets:
Define and own the Fleet Operations product strategy and roadmap

• Manage a multi-surface product roadmap spanning remote assistance, dispatch, and fleet management
Serve as the voice of the customer by continuously gathering and synthesizing feedback from airline/airport customers and internal operators to inform priorities
Scope phased product milestones that unlock value and provide instrumentation to enable data-driven iterative development over time

Drive technical execution across real-time and infrastructure-heavy systems

• Partner with Systems Engineering to decompose product needs into system requirements, test plans, and acceptance criteria
Participate in system design discussions with Infrastructure teams - ensure technical architectures are aligned with product needs and operational realities
Work with Program Management to ensure roadmap commitments are tracked, blockers are surfaced early, and dependencies are known
Prioritize the product backlog, balancing new features, technical debt, and bug fixes to ensure efficient development

Provide cross-functional leadership

• Serve as the primary Point of Contact and Subject Matter Expert for Fleet Operations products

sections.title: About the role
paras: As a Product Manager for DefenseOS, you will own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for a defense operating system derived directly from Applied Intuition's commercial automotive VehicleOS product, as the product peer to a director-level engineering lead. You will drive the product through customer discovery, requirements definition, prioritization, and close partnership with engineering, design, and operations — owning outcomes through influence rather than managing a team.

As the first instantiation of this broadly applicable defense product, you will own the product for a navy warship operating system that integrates combat systems, communications systems, and hull, mechanical, and electrical (HM&E) systems on unmanned surface vessels and traditional surface combatants. A central part of the work is shaping the product strategy for a zonal architecture — location-based zone controllers and centralized compute replacing a federated, domain-based design — and defining how it integrates with existing defense-unique systems built by primes that were not delivered with modernized software and data interfaces. Your work will influence the scope, sequencing, field-readiness, and adoption of the DefenseOS product.

sections.title: At Applied Intuition, you will
paras: This is an individual-contributor role: you own the product and drive outcomes through influence across engineering, design, and operations — without direct reports.
bullets: Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for DefenseOS — defining how Applied's commercial VehicleOS is adapted into a navy warship operating system, the first instantiation of this broadly applicable defense product.

Lead customer and user discovery directly with Navy program offices, operators, and crews to translate operational needs, acquisition requirements, and field constraints into a prioritized product roadmap.
Write clear requirements, define success metrics, and make the prioritization and scope trade-offs that keep engineering focused on the highest-value, field-relevant work.

Partner closely with engineering, hardware/integration, and operations to sequence delivery across simulation, integration lab, and live-platform testing on unmanned surface vessels and traditional surface combatants.
Own the trade-offs between speed, quality, and scope under acquisition and field constraints.
Work with design to shape operator interfaces and workflows grounded in how crews actually operate.
Partner with defense customers and shipbuilders/integrators as a design-informed product lead, translating their needs into the roadmap.
Communicate product strategy, status, risk, and trade-offs to senior leadership and external stakeholders, and provide product input into program and business decisions.

8+ years of product management experience shipping complex technical products, including owning a product line end to end, ideally platforms spanning both hardware and software, real-time/embedded, or systems-of-systems.
Demonstrated ability to own a product end to end as an individual contributor: vision, roadmap, requirements, prioritization, launch, and iteration against measurable outcomes.
Thrives as an IC — comfortable owning a product area and driving cross-functional outcomes through influence rather than managing direct reports.

Strong technical literacy — enough to engage credibly with engineers on architecture trade-offs (e.g., zonal versus federated domain architectures, hardware/software integration, interfaces and data flow) and make informed scope decisions, without managing the implementation.

Experience defining product strategy for integrating with legacy, proprietary, or closed third-party systems that lack modern software and data interfaces — deciding what to bridge and how to sequence the integration work.
Skilled at customer and user discovery: translating ambiguous operational problems into clear, prioritized requirements.
Comfort in a fast-paced, highly ambiguous environment, and the ability to make and defend trade-offs between speed, quality, and scope.

ashby:assorthealth:79c72fb7-e53e-4827-a6.summary:
Every time you call a doctor's office, the system forgets you the moment you hang up. You wait on hold, explain everything from scratch, get bounced between lines, and hope someone follows up. Everyone has felt this. No one should have to.

At Assort Health, we're building one continuous conversation for every patient. An AI agent that knows who you are, remembers how you like to be reached, and carries that context from your first symptom to your full recovery. What began as the first voice AI agent to schedule a specialty appointment has become the largest proprietary specialty dataset in healthcare: 345 million patient interactions, 62,000 care protocols, 1.6 million decision pathways.

sections.title: Building Healthcare That Remembers
paras: We went from 15 people in 2025 and will cross 250 by the end of 2026. Revenue is up 20x in 15 months and we've raised $222 million, including a recent $120 million Series C at a $1.2 billion valuation from investors including Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed. We've also been named to the Forbes Cloud 100 and the 2026 Enterprise Tech 30 as the only healthcare AI company on the list!
Healthcare spends $1.1 trillion a year on administration instead of care. If you want to help change that, apply below.

sections.title: Lead Development of High-Performance AI Agents
paras: As a Senior Product Manager, you’ll partner with engineering, design, and customers to build production-grade AI systems that manage high-volume, high-complexity interactions. You’ll be responsible for taking agents from concept to launch and continuously improving them as new business needs emerge. You will scope out new products and surface area end to end, leading the charge on new product workstreams 0→1. You’ll work directly with the CEO on a small yet quickly growing product team. Your work will directly improve healthcare access and the lives of both patients and providers.

sections.title: Work Directly With Customers
paras: You will engage deeply with customers: across technical, operational, and executive teams, to:
bullets: Understand workflows, requirements, and bottlenecks
Design and present demos that showcase our capabilities
Collaborate with technical stakeholders to solve integration challenges
Tailor and refine agents so they align with real business processes
Serve as a strategic advisor, helping customers shape long-term AI strategies
Build strong, trusted relationships across customer organizations

sections.title: Influence the Product Roadmap
paras: You’ll work with cross-functional partners to define requirements, prioritize features, and translate customer needs into actionable engineering work. You’ll help ensure we’re building the right capabilities at the right time to support our next phase of product growth: moving beyond just answering the phone.

We are launching proactive, agentic campaigns to close care gaps—reaching out to patients to schedule things like annual physicals and flu shots rather than waiting for them to react to health needs. We are also deploying Agent Memory to ensure every conversation feels personal. Our system uses past interactions to predict a patient’s needs: remembering if they prefer Spanish, adjusting speaking speed, or modulating voice tone to be more empathetic based on context.

But modern patient access isn’t just about voice. We are meeting patients where they are by expanding into chatbots and two-way texting. We are also fixing hidden friction in the background with our new referral orchestration and document processing platforms, ensuring that critical data is ingested automatically so patients get the care they need faster.

ashby:atticus:c9c2a0a8-4049-4c19-932f-b3.summary:
At any given time, 16 million Americans are experiencing a crisis that requires urgent help from our legal system or government. The right assistance could transform their lives. But today, most never get it.

Atticus makes it easy for any sick or injured American to get life-changing aid. Our mission is to tear down barriers between people in crisis and the aid they deserve. In the last six years, we’ve become the leading platform connecting people with disabilities to government benefits.

We also help victims of accidents, misconduct, and violence get compensation from insurance. So far, we’ve helped hundreds of thousands of people access over $10 billion in life-changing aid —and earned over 20,000 five-star reviews. And we’re just getting started.

sections.title: About Atticus
paras: We've raised more than $100 million from top VC firms like Forerunner, Google Ventures, and True Ventures, and we’re on our way to creating a category defining business assisting Americans in need.

sections.title: The Job
paras: Each day, hundreds of people seek our help getting disability benefits or insurance compensation. They’re intimidated by the process, unsure where to turn, and desperate for good advice.

As part of our Client Experience team, your job is to get them on the right path. You’ll spend each day communicating on the phone with clients to understand their situation, figure out whether we can help them, and advise them on the next steps. You'll become an expert on a complex and interesting field, learn to rapidly navigate our internal tech platforms and tools (Salesforce, etc.), and help hundreds of ordinary people (each with a unique story) every week. You’ll be measured by and compensated for the impact you have on our clients.

This job is different from traditional customer service or sales: Our service is totally free, and clients are desperate for our help — so you'll rarely talk to an angry customer. The conversations are deeply rewarding, and clients are profoundly grateful. You will have to navigate conversations on deeply personal and sad topics, gently but quickly offer guidance, and handle many different interactions over the course of a day.

sections.title: Qualifications
paras: We are strongly committed to building a diverse team. If you’re from a background that’s underrepresented in tech, we’d love to meet you.
bullets: You have at least three years of professional work experience, and have succeeded in jobs that involve talking to customers all day (CX, sales, support, hospitality, etc.).
You care about people and can interact with folks from all walks of life; you’re able to simultaneously be supportive to a person in crisis and quickly drive a conversation.
You’re a quick learner and a competent writer, able to master complex new topics and platforms when given instruction and support.
You’ve had a metrics-driven role and you exceeded the goals set for you and outperformed your peers.
You've previously worked at high volume, high-performing service/sales/support team from a company known for great customer service.

sections.title: Location
paras: This job is fully remote and we’re committed to empowering everyone with flexibility. We care a lot about building a great culture and we think some interactions need to happen in person, so we put a lot of thought into retreats, offsites, and other ways to gather.

The role involves counseling individual and corporate fiduciaries, beneficiaries, high-net-worth families, and closely held business owners through every stage of trust and estate settlement.

The primary focus of this position is trust and estate administration and settlement. The successful candidate will serve as the day-to-day point person on fiduciary administration matters, managing client matters with a high degree of autonomy. Estate planning experience is valued as a complementary skill set, and the practice offers opportunities to advise on planning matters as well.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Own and manage a full docket of trust administration, probate, and estate settlement matters from intake to closing, serving as the primary attorney and day-to-day contact for fiduciaries and families

Guide personal representatives and trustees through all phases of administration, including marshaling, valuing, and retitling assets; paying debts, expenses, and claims; and making interim and final distributions

Handle supervised and unsupervised estate administrations and trust-related court proceedings. This includes petitions, statutory notices, inventories, accountings, petitions for distribution, and closing filings
Interpret wills, trust instruments, and related governing documents. Advise on fiduciary powers, duties, and discretionary distribution decisions
Counsel individual and corporate fiduciaries on fiduciary duties, beneficiary communications, conflict avoidance, and risk management, including releases, receipts, and settlement agreements

Coordinate post-mortem tax planning and compliance, including estate tax returns (Form 706), fiduciary income tax returns (Form 1041), portability and other elections, basis issues, and gift and GST tax matters. Work closely with CPAs, fiduciary accountants, and appraisers

Identify and resolve administration issues such as trust modification, decanting, nonjudicial settlement agreements, disclaimers, and beneficiary or creditor disputes. Work with the firm’s litigation colleagues when matters become contested
Oversee the administration of closely held business interests, real estate, and other complex or illiquid assets held in estates and trusts

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: J.D. from an accredited law school and strong academic credentials

Substantial, senior-level experience (generally 10 or more years) in trust and estate administration, probate, and estate settlement, gained in a law firm, bank or trust company fiduciary department, family office, or similar sophisticated fiduciary setting

Proven ability to independently manage a high-volume, complex administration and settlement docket at a level comparable to a trust and estate administration partner or senior trust/estate settlement officer
Deep working knowledge of probate procedure, trust law, fiduciary duties, and post-death administration. Experience with Indiana probate and trust practice is strongly preferred
Strong command of estate, gift, generation-skipping transfer, and fiduciary income tax principles as they apply to administration
Experience advising individual and corporate fiduciaries, beneficiaries, and high-net-worth families, including those with closely held business interests
Estate planning drafting experience is a plus but not required
Exposure to fiduciary litigation, tax audits, or tax controversy matters is a plus

ashby:benchling:13d16488-e9f4-4c1c-baad-.summary:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is…

sections.title: ROLE OVERVIEW
paras: Benchling is building a world-class Professional Services team to drive implementations for our rapidly expanding customer base. Implementation Managers work with our customers, from small Biotech startups to the largest BioPharmas in the world to develop a deep understanding of their R&D Processes, and roll out solutions that transform how their research teams work together.

To be successful in this role, you will leverage your scientific background, project management skills, and product expertise to drive successful implementations of the Benchling platform. You will work hand in hand with the research scientists at our customers, and teams throughout Benchling to implement our solutions, and ensure our customers are successful. Implementation Managers lead all aspects of customer rollouts from requirements analysis and solution design, to configurations, testing, training, and onboarding users onto the system.

sections.title: RESPONSIBILITIES
bullets: Manage initial rollouts for new Benchling customers as well as expansion projects with new teams or for new processes at existing customers.
Own implementation success from project kickoff to go-live, leveraging strong project management skills, scientific expertise, and deep product knowledge.
Build and execute detailed project plans, own project activities, work with other team members to execute on project deliverables to ensure on time, on budget, high quality deployments.
Understand customers' scientific workflows and determine how Benchling can best be leveraged to meet their key business needs.
Lead requirements and design workshops, perform data modeling & application configuration, develop test plans and guide UAT execution, train and onboard users.
Act as a trusted advisor for customers, guiding them through the implementation ensuring they leverage and apply Benchling Best Practices.
Understand and document customer pain points, advocate for them internally to influence product changes.
Develop and optimize enterprise training programs including written and video collateral.

sections.title: QUALIFICATIONS
bullets: Degree in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Immunology, Bioinformatics, Biological Engineering or a related field. Advanced degrees preferred.
At least 2 years of experience in a lab or research setting. You must be able to empathize with scientists and quickly understand complicated scientific concepts.
Strong communication skills. You must be able to quickly and effectively connect with a range of stakeholders, including scientists, IT project leads, and executives.
Self-starter with the ability to be successful in a startup environment.
Curious, creative, and tenacious. You should be excited to collaborate with customers and other Benchling teammates as a thought partner.
Ability to travel up to 25% based on customer and project needs.

Managing this well requires two things in parallel: ensuring OT teams can easily build integrations with IT systems without friction, and maintaining a healthy process by which extensions are proposed, triaged, and absorbed into the roadmap rather than accumulating as one-off customizations.

The response isn’t to double down on features — it’s to make HiveMQ the default substrate for operational agents, the only choice that compounds into Intelligence and Agentic AI in ways no alternative can match. sections.title: About the Role
paras: We're hiring a Technical Product Manager to be our product’s right hand as Osmo scales its Software and AI organization. This is a hands-on product role, not a program management role — you'll own scoping, requirements, and delivery negotiation directly, working independently from day one.

Your first mandate: Osmo's internal workflows are largely manual today, and information doesn't always flow through our systems the way it should. You'll identify the 3-5 tools that would drive 80% of the impact, embed with the relevant teams to master the problem, and come out with clear requirements that get built. From there, expect to move across workstreams as priorities shift, applying the same structural skills to a new domain. You'll work closely with engineering throughout, and you'll need to hold your own there: when an estimate doesn't add up, you push back with specifics, ask for the breakdown, and know how to simplify a requirement to get something shipped faster. This role takes real tenacity to drive scope and delivery under ambiguity, and real kindness in how you ask a stretched engineering team for more.

sections.title: What You'll Do:
bullets: Scope With Rigor — Independently scope projects end to end: understand the business value and customer need, then write clear, complete requirements that inform what engineering builds.

Negotiate Scope and Estimates — When an engineering estimate doesn't match reality, push back with tenacity: ask for the breakdown, identify what's actually driving the cost, and simplify or revise the requirement to get to a faster, leaner build.
Find the 80% — Scope Osmo's highest-value internal tooling opportunities: identify the 3-5 tools that would drive the majority of workflow impact, then sequence and prioritize the build.
Embed and Master — Rapidly insert yourself into a workstream, understand it deeply, and come out with the requirements and plan to fix what's broken.
Partner Directly With Engineering — Work hand-in-hand with the CTO’s team to get scoped work built and delivered against committed dates.

Operate Without a Script — Take high-level direction into an ambiguous space and bring back clarity, milestones, and a plan — with the curiosity to figure out what's actually needed rather than waiting to be told.
Bring Structure Without Bureaucracy — Sequence and manage ambiguous initiatives without adding process for its own sake.
Pivot With the Business — Move fluidly across workstreams as Osmo's priorities shift, applying the same core PM skill set to new problems.

sections.title: Who You Are:
bullets: A Mid-Senior Generalist — You work independently and bring PM best practices without needing to be trained on the fundamentals. You're a generalist, not a specialist: your skills are fungible, and you're comfortable being reassigned to a completely different problem space.

Direct Engineering Collaboration, Non-Negotiable — You have worked hands-on with engineering teams in a prior role. You know how to sit across from an engineering lead, question an estimate, and land on a scope that actually reflects the work.
A Real Requirements Writer — Writing requirements documents has been a core, sustained part of at least one prior role — not a one-off exercise.
Comfortable in Ambiguity — You can take a loosely defined problem and a high-level directive and figure out the rest. You don't need a detailed plan handed to you.

A Clear, Confident Communicator — You can bridge business needs and engineering constraints, and you're comfortable pushing back on senior stakeholders, including leadership, when timelines, scope, or resources don't add up.
An AI-Native Operator — Fluency with modern AI tools (LLMs, automation platforms, workflow builders), with a track record of using them in your own work.
Bachelor's degree or higher, or equivalent experience.

sections.title: ABOUT PEARLY
paras: That's what makes Pearly feel different. The caliber of the people and the intentionality behind how we operate.

sections.title: THE ROLE
paras: You'll own Practice Experience: the app the practice team works in every day, the workflows inside it, and the experience around it from onboarding to daily use. Your users are the people responsible for a practice's financial performance, some living in Pearly for hours a day working a queue of accounts, others, like an owner or a CFO, checking in weekly and needing to know where things stand without digging. And it isn't one customer. It's the single-location office running its own billing, the group or DSO standardizing across dozens of locations, and the outsourced billing company working on behalf of hundreds. You own that arc for all of them without building three versions of the product.

The problems are concrete. A new customer should get live and start collecting in days, not weeks. An RCM manager should be able to set up a payment plan in under a minute without calling support. A balance sitting 60 days past due shouldn't wait for a person to decide to chase it. And a DSO rolling out location 41 shouldn't need the hand-holding location 1 did. Some of those are workflow problems, some are product we haven't built, and some are automation that should have replaced the work entirely. All of them compound directly into collections.

Part of your roadmap exists to win customers and part exists to keep them, and you should know which is which. The metrics you'll answer for are listed below. Senior here means you own it end to end, from discovery through release, without day-to-day direction. The lines around your area are thin on purpose. sections.title: WHAT YOU'LL OWN

The Daily Workflow, and Automating It Away. How staff find an account, understand a balance, decide what needs attention today, take action, and trust what they see. The job underneath it is chasing money that's owed across thousands of accounts, usually while the phone is ringing. Make that work faster where a person has to do it, and build the automation and the new products that mean they don't.

sections.title: WHAT YOU'LL BE MEASURED ON

Landing new DSOs and practices (MRR). The product gaps that decide acquiring new DSOs and practices, and the permissions, reporting, and multi-location behavior that make us credible with a DSO. Measured by new offices landed and billed, and by the deals where product was the deciding factor.

Quick ROI and expanding offices. Time to value is the quickest win in dental and it's yours: days from contract to live and to first dollar collected, pilot-to-billed conversion, offices taken live per implementation person, and how fast a group gets from pilot to full rollout.

ashby:siro:e36e5996-349f-4daa-9ccb-105c4.summary:
Field sales powers the economy — but most teams are struggling. Reps are buried in admin work, managers are stretched thin, and leaders can’t see what’s really happening in the field.

Siro is redefining how field sales teams learn, perform, and win.

We started as an AI-powered coaching platform that helped reps improve their outcomes in the field.

Today, we’re something much bigger — an intelligent companion that automates sales reps’ tedious admin work, gives managers real-time visibility, and helps executives see around corners.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
paras: We're looking for a Staff Product Manager to own meaningful pieces of Siro end-to-end — across AI, data ingestion, proactive agents, integrations, and the experiences customers touch every day.

Siro is building the intelligence layer for the enormous part of the economy that still runs on in-person conversation — an in-person workforce most software has ignored. We capture what happens in the field and turn it into intelligence our users act on daily — prepping a rep before a meeting, surfacing the next move, handling the follow-up.

Your job is to push that arc forward: make the intelligence sharper, make people trust it, and close the gap between insight and action. You'll own real problems the whole way, from ambiguous idea to a product customers rely on.
bullets: Own and ship end-to-end . Drive strategy and product concepts through discovery, launch, adoption, and iteration. You're on the hook for whether it provides value, not just whether it shipped.

Build for someone who doesn't sit at a desk. Our users are in trucks, driveways, and showrooms. We believe that we should never add work to a rep's day — the product has to earn its place, which makes this a harder and more interesting design problem to solve.

Be a forward-deployed PM. Our customers run businesses that look very different from ours and likely from any you’ve ever worked in. You'll get on the plane, ride along on calls, sit with managers onsite, listen to conversations, and turn what you learn across industries into one coherent product.

Move Siro from insight to action . Apply our intelligence to drive behavior change and operate the sales motion — prep before a conversation, the next move surfaced in the moment, the follow-up handled. This is where the product is heading, and you'll build it.
Raise the AI quality bar. Accuracy, citations, speaker attribution, latency, trust, the weird edge cases. A demo that impresses is easy; a tool a skeptical rep opens every morning is the actual job.

sections.title: Requirements / Who You Are
bullets: 9+ years in product management , including ownership of meaningful product areas at a growth-stage company.

You're a “ barrel.” Give you an ambiguous problem and you create momentum: figure out what matters, talk to the right customers, pull the data, make the tradeoffs, align the team, and get something valuable shipped. You don’t need a clean brief or constant direction to turn a vague opportunity into a real product.
Sound product judgment in messy domains . You're comfortable when the inputs are imperfect and there's no obvious right answer, and you pull the right people together to make good decisions.

Bias to action and doing whatever it takes. If you see friction in the UX or a customer complains about something on a call that you think is worth fixing — it’s not a ticket to an engineering backlog, you write the code and ship it.
Obsessed with customers and details. You'd take a day in the field over a day in a planning doc, and you make it happen without being asked.
Enough technical fluency to dig into the tradeoffs with engineering. model quality, latency vs. cost per query, and how fresh integration data really needs to be.

You carry product vision with you everywhere. You have strong taste, you think in systems, and you can connect today’s bug, customer ask, or workflow edge case to where the product needs to go over the next few years.

sections.title: What is this role about?

As Senior Product Manager, Identity at Bondora, you'll own the whole stack and the platform that runs it, on a team you're building from the ground up. This isn't a maintenance function: Bondora operates across seven European markets and is pursuing a massive, multibillion-euro consumer credit opportunity. Every one of those markets runs on knowing who the customer is and whether we're clear to serve them, which makes this one of the most consequential systems in the company, not a back-office afterthought.

You'll build the policy and platform for KYC, AML, sanctions screening, and customer data privacy, and execute it alongside Legal, Risk, AML Operations, and Engineering, building one of the sharpest identity-and-compliance product functions in European fintech from the ground up. We build product-first and AI-first here: starting from what the problem actually requires, not automating whatever process already exists.

sections.title: Your main responsibilities:
bullets: Define KYC, AML, and sanctions-screening policy together with Legal and Risk, so the rest of the business, Credit, Growth, Banking, can expand into new markets and products without re-litigating what's legally allowed every time.

Run AML and enhanced due diligence case management end to end with the AML operations team and Engineering: the workflows, the escalation paths, and an audit trail that actually holds up under regulator scrutiny.

Set data-privacy compliance for customer identity together with Legal, GDPR retention, data subject rights, the legal-basis register, the single source every team touching customer data relies on instead of re-deriving it themselves.

Direct product-first, AI-first automation together with Engineering: redesign how KYC and AML review should work rather than bolting automation onto today's manual process, replacing it with decisioning that's both automated and auditable, so the business scales without scaling headcount linearly.
Build the Identity & Customer Data Platform together with Engineering and the teams who depend on it, creating one source of truth about our customers.

You're joining early: the Identity team is being bootstrapped, which means real room to shape how it operates, who's on it, and how it works with the rest of Product, not inheriting someone else's structure.

sections.title: The Team
paras: At Learning Commons, we operate at the intersection of technology, research, and philanthropy. We pair product development with grantmaking to scale proven teaching and learning practices for the benefit of every learner. We aim to bring learning science into the tools educators and students use every day.

Our work is grounded in a deep belief: when technology reflects the realities of classrooms and the science of how students learn, it can meaningfully strengthen teaching and unlock new possibilities for students. The rise of generative AI offers us a once-in-a-generation opportunity to dramatically accelerate the translation of research insights into practical, classroom-ready tools; tools that honor teachers’ expertise, adapt to students’ needs, and make effective learning practices easier to access, implement, and sustain.

In today’s fragmented edtech landscape, school districts are often left piecing together products that don’t always align with curricula or instructional needs. While AI holds enormous potential to support teachers and students, it can only deliver on that promise when grounded in research, high-quality educational data, and expert evaluation. That’s why we’re building open, public-purpose infrastructure — datasets, rubrics, and resources — that help raise the standard for educational tools and create more consistent, impactful learning experiences for all students and teachers.

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: We are seeking a Product Manager for a 12-month fixed-term position on the Knowledge Graph team. As a Product Manager on the Knowledge Graph team, you'll help build the data layer for AI in education. AI tools for teachers and students are only as good as the data behind them — and the data they need sits scattered across incompatible formats, academic journals, and proprietary systems, so developers spend their time stitching sources together instead of building. The Knowledge Graph turns that fragmented material into structured, queryable infrastructure — connecting what students are expected to learn, the materials they learn from, and the research on how they learn best, all grounded in learning science.

This is a chance to shape a foundation that's still being built. As the graph expands into new subjects and kinds of data, you'll help decide what it covers and how much developers can rely on it, putting you at the center of how research-grounded AI reaches classrooms. It's a rare product surface — few roles combine data modeling, developer experience, and public-purpose education data in one seat — and it rewards a PM who likes to be hands-on and close to the details. You'll have real ownership from the start, with room to grow as the graph scales.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own datasets end to end — Take each dataset from acquisition and licensing through modeling, ingestion, and launch. Write the product docs that define the work clearly enough for engineering to build and ship without rework.

Partner with our users — Work closely with the developers and build partners who use the graph to understand their needs and where they get stuck, and spot opportunities for the graph to solve those problems. Help shape the API surfaces they build on, across the REST API and beyond.

Plan the work, short and long term — Use partner evidence to shape the roadmap — which data to bring in and how it should grow — and plan the near-term work with engineering so the team ships against a clear, current plan.

Work hands-on in the data — Open the source data yourself, run coverage and gap analyses, and verify what ships against the source. Decide how a new source maps onto the graph, when to reuse the model and when to extend it, and set clear, testable acceptance criteria engineers can build against.
Keep the cross-functional team aligned — Work across engineering, Trust, partnerships, tech writers, and marketing to move each launch forward and keep everyone working from the same plan.

sections.title: What You'll Bring
bullets: 3–5 years of product management experience with a track record of shipping, preferably data products, APIs, or developer-facing platforms

Education or edtech grounding — You've built products in education or worked in the field, and you understand how curricula, academic standards, and classrooms work well enough to judge what developers serving schools actually need

Works well with deep technical experts — You partner with engineers and data experts as a credible peer: you ask sharp questions, pressure-test tradeoffs, and write up complex technical decisions clearly enough for developers to build on

Hands-on data fluency and modeling judgment — You personally open raw data files (JSONL, CSV), write queries (SQL, Cypher, or similar), and pull your own counts rather than delegating the check; you can reason about entities and relationships, sketch the nodes and edges for a new dataset, and tell a data gap from a modeling gap
Strong product sense — You understand what the people building on your product are trying to do and where they get stuck, and turn that into priorities

It’s because back in middle school, you didn't just run the bake sale—you single-handedly negotiated end-cap shelf space with the principal, convinced the local grocery store to donate supplies, and turned a $50 budget into a massive multi-thousand-dollar fundraising empire. You didn’t just sell cookies; you owned the distribution network.

That rare mix of big-picture strategy, ruthless retail charm, and absolute operational mastery makes you the ultimate retail mastermind we need to tackle the absolute big dogs: Target and Dick’s Sporting Goods (DSG). In this role, you’ll act as both the strategic visionary and the high-energy account owner, making sure our sunglasses dominate the shelves, our inventory moves like wildfire, and our retail partners view us as their absolute favorite, can't-live-without brand. So channel that powerhouse retail energy and apply today to be goodr’s Senior National Account Manager!

Translate sell-through data and retail math into killer commercial strategies that close forecast gaps before they even happen
Serve as the ultimate internal connective tissue across Sales, Operations, Supply Chain, and Digital to execute account wins flawlessly

sections.title: About Product Management:
paras: As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own your product’s roadmap, collateral, and market research, and you will collaborate with Grafana leadership on fine-tuning your product’s goals. You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential.

Product Managers are the bridge that connect Engineering, Design, and UX to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.

sections.title: The opportunity:
paras: As the Product Manager for Application Observability (App O11y), you’ll be responsible for helping application developers and SREs understand how their applications are performing, what’s affecting their users, and where to focus when something goes wrong. You’ll continue to build App O11y on top of the Knowledge Graph and fully integrate high-fidelity signals like traces and profiles, making all three first-class parts of the product experience. You’ll bring these capabilities together into our full-stack observability experience, alongside our Drilldown products, while building AI-first workflows that help customers investigate issues, understand root cause, and take action beyond static experiences.

Your primary responsibility will be to define the vision and roadmap that takes App O11y into its next wave of adoption and revenue growth. This will require heavy customer discovery, using product data to understand where users get stuck, and working with your engineering and design partners to turn those needs into clear priorities. You’ll balance new product opportunities with the depth, performance, and reliability customers need from tracing and profiling, while working across R&D to ensure App O11y is tightly woven into our broader Grafana Cloud suite.

You’ll also work closely with PMM and GTM to help customers understand the value of App O11y. This includes shaping pricing and packaging that make it easy to get started and grow with the product. You’ll regularly review customer feedback and usage data to understand what’s working and where people get stuck, and then be accountable for turning what you learn into stronger adoption and revenue growth.
bullets: Transform ideas and feedback into a product vision and roadmap

Work closely with PMM to enable GTM on product differentiation, including creating and updating presentations, documentation, website content, datasheets, and whitepapers.

sections.title: Director of Product, Payments
paras: Guild is hiring a Director of Product, Payments, to lead the team building how money moves across Guild. You'll own the strategy for Guild's payment network - the infrastructure that funds education between employers, Guild, and learning providers - and lead a team of product managers expanding our offering to a flexible menu of payment modalities that expands Guild’s ability to meet discrete finance needs in the context of a benefit. This is a leadership role with a broad remit: defining payment network strategy, leading a world-class team, and building the core of a product that impacts millions of learners in the US.

To be eligible, you must have established experience building payments products before at a payments company, a fintech, or a platform that embedded card issuing and money movement into its product. The ideal candidate has done that work on a global scale. You bring a sharp point of view on payments economics, a willingness to challenge the status quo, and the commercial and financial fluency to be a true partner to Finance, Commercial, and the leadership team. If that sounds like you, read on!

sections.title: What You'll Do
paras: Global Scale. Build capability sets with a global-first approach, serving as a subject matter expert on globalization, including specific expertise around currency handling, localization, and international markets.
bullets: Team Leadership : Lead, coach, and grow a team of product managers across payment modalities and platform capabilities. Set the bar for product craft, build a strong operating rhythm, and develop PMs into leaders.

Zero-to-One and Scale : Guide the team from concept through vendor selection, pilot, and scale - shipping quickly, learning, and iterating - while knowing when to step in on high-stakes decisions and when to let the team run.
AI-Native Product Development : Set the expectation that your team builds and operates with AI where appropriate, and identify where AI materially improves the product itself, and at what level.

Vendor & Network Partnerships : Help facilitate Guild's relationships with processors, card networks, and money movement partners. Assist commercial negotiations on economics, SLAs, and roadmap alignment, and manage the partner portfolio over time.
Payments Economics & Pricing : Partner with stakeholders on pricing, packaging, and business cases; challenge assumptions and bring an informed outside perspective to Guild’s monetization strategy.

Cross-Functional Leadership : Represent payments strategy in executive and leadership-level conversations. Align Engineering, Finance, Legal, Commercial, and Operations around a shared roadmap, and resolve trade-offs across them.

Compliance, Risk & Program Governance : Partner with Legal, Compliance, and Finance to set the governance framework for card issuing and money movement - spend controls, reconciliation, settlement, fraud prevention, and program oversight - and make sure the team builds to it.
Funding Service Optimization : Set and drive the strategy for Guild's funding service, improving speed, reliability, working capital efficiency, and cost per transaction.

sections.title: What You'll Bring
paras: Guild partners with the country’s most innovative employers, including Chipotle, Target, Walgreens, JPMorgan Chase, Hilton, Spectrum, PepsiCo, Tyson, and more, to build the talent needed for today and a resilient workforce for tomorrow. Guild helps employers identify, develop, and mobilize internal talent, enabling workers to gain skills for in-demand roles and companies to stay agile.

By connecting employees to real-world learning, coaching, and career support, and providing companies with actionable talent insights, Guild transforms all talent into high-impact contributors and positions companies for long-term, sustainable growth. For more information, visit https://www.guild.com .

Guild is a female-founded, certified B Corp. The company has been recognized by Fortune’s Change the World list (2021, 2025), the Forbes Cloud 100 (2020–2025), Great Place to Work (2022–2025), CNBC’s Disruptor 50 (2021–2024), TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies (2022), Inc.’s Best-Led Companies (2021), Fast Company’s World Changing Ideas (2020), and B Lab’s Best for the World (2019), among many others.
bullets: Experience : 10+ years of product management experience, including significant time building payments products - card issuing, virtual cards, money movement, or B2B payment flows - at a fintech or payments company or in an embedded payments role at a platform company. Bonus if this experience has been global.
People Leadership : 5+ years managing product managers, with a track record of developing PMs, running a healthy team, and raising the quality bar.
Payments Domain Depth : Fluency in the mechanics of card issuing and money movement, and the vendor ecosystem behind them. Experience with cross-border payments is a plus.

Strategic Track Record : Demonstrated success setting and executing a multi-year payments strategy, including business case building, and taking products from zero to launch and scaling through ambiguity.

Deal-Making : Experience facilitating third-party vendor and network partnerships end to end - sourcing, negotiating, and managing them - and partnering with commercial and legal teams on terms and economics.

Financial Fluency : Comfort building and defending financial models; able to work as a peer with Finance on unit economics, pricing, and working capital, and to challenge the status quo when the numbers say so.
Technical Fluency : Able to go deep with engineers on API design, integration architecture, and build-vs-buy trade-offs; engineering leaders trust your judgment and instincts.

AI Fluency : You use AI tools daily in your own work and have a point of view on where they change how product teams operate. You can separate the real opportunities in payments (risk, reconciliation, support, emerging agentic payment flows) from the hype, and you hold your team to a high bar for using it well.

Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.

Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.

This dedicated team of problem solvers ensures that every customer interaction is handled with care, empathy, and expertise. Operating across multiple channels, they provide timely and effective solutions to customer inquiries and issues. The team plays a critical role in maintaining our reputation for exceptional service while gathering valuable insights that help improve our products and services. As we continue to scale, we're looking for a visionary leader who can elevate our support operations while nurturing a positive, high-performance culture among our support teams.

In 1949, as Diners Club tells it, Frank McNamara finished dinner in Manhattan and found his wallet at home in another suit. His wife came down and paid. He returned to the same table the following February and settled the bill with a piece of cardboard, honored at twenty-seven restaurants and carried by two hundred people, most of them his friends. A year later there were 42,000.

McNamara solved two problems at once. Acceptance: enough restaurants to make the card worth carrying, and enough diners to make it worth accepting. And credit: thirty unsecured days of it, on nothing but a signature. The networks settled acceptance decades ago. What is left is the credit, and the question of why someone carries this card rather than another one. That is this role.

paras: Our pre-sales team helps some of the largest organizations in the world find and close experience gaps with the Qualtrics XM Data & AI Platform, which combines experience management (XM) data with artificial intelligence (AI) to predict what comes next and act on it.

As a Senior Principal Solution Consultant in North America Enterprise (NA ENT), you will partner with our Sales Teams on our largest and most strategic opportunities to win both the technical decision and the business case. You bring the product depth to show what the platform can do and the strategic perspective to help executives decide what to do with it. While most of your efforts will be focused in the pre-sales environment, some of the additional cross-functional initiatives may include input in product direction, content generation, contributing to analyst reports/relationships and attending marketing events.

Building and showcasing world-class product demonstrations to highlight the value of Qualtrics products in unique, compelling and creative ways.
Winning the technical decision and the business case on complex, multi-stakeholder deals.
Contributing to team outcomes, including win rate, pipeline, net new annual recurring revenue (ARR), customer satisfaction and strategy for key accounts.
Raising the bar for the team by sharing what works and helping your peers grow.

sections.title: How You’ll Grow
bullets: Learning the full XM platform, including customer experience, employee experience and market research, and the AI capabilities that connect them.
Deepen your expertise in AI and data and shape how customers apply them to business outcomes.

Grow as a leader through mentoring, deal coaching and cross-functional initiatives, with a career action plan built alongside your manager.
As we build an AI-first company and change the market for Experience Management, you will be at the cutting edge of this transformation in enterprise software.

Mentor peers through deal reviews, demonstration feedback and shared asset development.

greenhouse:rithum:8394229.summary:
Rithum™ is the world’s most trusted commerce network, accelerating how brands, suppliers, and retailers work together to deliver seamless e-commerce experiences. We provide an unmatched platform for brands and retailers, enabling them to accelerate growth, optimize operations across channels, scale product offerings and enhance margins.

Today, more than 40,000 companies trust Rithum to grow their business across hundreds of channels, representing over $50 billion in annual GMV. Using our commerce, marketing, and delivery solutions, our customers create optimized consumer shopping journeys from beginning to end.

sections.title: Overview
paras: As a Client Strategy Associate , you keep the daily operations of assigned Managed Marketplaces clients running as they launch and grow on major U.S. marketplaces. Working alongside Technical Account Managers (TAMs), you monitor listing health, resolve listing errors, turn listing data into daily and monthly reports, and keep launches, client sessions, and change requests on track. You are the day-to-day link between the TAMs and Rithum’s managed services partner. You deliver accurate, on-time reports and raise issues, with a likely cause and owner, before they affect client sales. This role is designed as an entry point into Technical Account Management. With hands-on training from the TAM team and exposure to some of Rithum’s largest Managed Marketplaces clients, Client Strategy Associates build the skills to progress to Technical Account Manager and then Senior Technical Account Manager.

At Rithum, all team members are expected to leverage AI to work smarter, accelerate decision-making, automate repeatable work, and improve outcomes. You are encouraged to continuously identify opportunities to apply AI, data, and scalable processes to enhance productivity, drive innovation, and deliver greater value for our clients, partners, and teams while maintaining appropriate judgment, quality, security, and compliance.

sections.title: Responsibilities
paras: Partner Coordination & Account Continuity
bullets: Monitor daily listing and publication status across assigned marketplaces and alert TAMs to drops, including the likely cause and owner.
Resolve listing and publication errors in the Rithum platform, and escalate through Salesforce when needed.
Update content, taxonomy, attributes, and pricing to bring new marketplaces to 90% publication within one month and sustain 97% or higher.
Take products live within 3 business days of receiving complete data.
Build and deliver daily listing reports on time every business day.
Compile monthly KPI scorecards and channel health checks, and submit them to TAMs for review.
Prepare materials for weekly client sessions and for launch and optimization workshops, and support each launch through ramp-up and hypercare.
Prepare assigned accounts for peak and holiday periods, including seasonal coverage for Cyber 5.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: 1+ years of experience in e-commerce operations, client support, or data operations (internships count).
Experience using Excel or Google Sheets for data analysis, including formulas, lookups, and pivot tables.

Experience using AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Claude) to improve productivity through research, communication, analysis, documentation, automation, workflow optimization, and decision-making.
Strong attention to detail and clear written communication.
2+ years of experience in e-commerce operations, client support or data operations.
Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, or a related field.
Exposure to U.S. marketplaces (e.g., Amazon, Walmart, Target Plus).
Familiarity with product data and taxonomy.

greenhouse:starburst:5483176008.summary: Starburst delivers enterprise intelligence at scale by giving organizations secure, governed access to all their data, wherever it lives. Built for distributed data environments, Starburst helps enterprises power AI and analytics without the cost and complexity of traditional data consolidation. With open standards including Trino and Apache Iceberg, Starburst enables trusted access to complete enterprise context while helping organizations avoid vendor lock-in. Leading global enterprises trust Starburst to fuel AI, analytics, and enterprise intelligence. Learn more at starburst.ai .

sections.title: About the role
paras: Starburst query engine workloads focus on two things: making federated queries fast across every source, and being the best place to run Apache Iceberg. Connectors and catalogs sit under both. They decide the breadth of connectors and use cases supported, how metadata is read, and how well Iceberg tables behave in practice.
AI agents reason across the whole data estate and generate queries as they go, so performance has to come from the engine and connectors working well on queries nobody planned in advance.

We are seeking a Product Manager to own the existing connector portfolio and catalog strategy, keeping both reliable, current, and prioritized by customer demand. You will also contribute to performance work on federation, including automated and dynamic approaches that engineering is building across data sources.

sections.title: As Product Manager, Connectors and Federation at Starburst you will:
bullets: Own the roadmap and health of existing connectors, including database connectors and lake connectors such as Iceberg
Build new connectors where customer impact justifies it

Own the strategy for the flagship Starburst Metastore offering, along with ownership of other catalogs (HMS, Glue, REST catalogs such as Polaris, Unity Catalog, and others), with a focus on optionality rather than betting on one
Make federated queries faster by tracing slow queries to the responsible layer (engine, connector, or source) and turning findings into prioritized product work
Make Starburst the best place to run Iceberg by shaping read and write paths, table metadata handling, and catalog interoperability
Plan and prioritize performance enhancements for each connector based on customer demand, such as pushdown, type mapping, parallel reads, partition pruning, statistics, and metadata handling
Keep up to date with Trino spec changes and their impact on connectors and catalogs
Contribute to the automated, dynamic performance work across data sources, in partnership with engineering

sections.title: Some of the things we look for:
bullets: 3+ years as a Product Manager, with ownership of a technical infrastructure or data platform product
Hands on experience with a query engine: you have shipped or owned features on one, or built closely against one
Performance intuition: you ask for the plan before forming an opinion, and you can place a slowdown in the engine, the connector, or the source
Willingness to learn how connectors differ from one another, and to direct engineering toward the specific features that matter most for each
Working knowledge of object storage and the lakehouse, with a focus on Apache Iceberg
Working understanding of what a catalog does and the tradeoffs between HMS, Glue, and REST catalogs
Exposure to more than one source type, and awareness that type systems, limits, and consistency differ per source
Engineering credibility: you read docs, issues, and pull requests, and are comfortable with open source engine communities

greenhouse:storable:6210274004.summary: At Storable, we're redefining property management for specialty real estate. Powered by AI and three decades of industry data, Storable empowers over 33,000 self-storage facilities with the industry's only fully integrated technology platform. Our end-to-end solutions—from management software and demand generation to CRM tools and delinquency solutions—help storage operators streamline workflows, attract tenants, and grow revenue. Dedicated to empowering self-storage owners and operators, Storable helps you Win More every day. Explore our platform solutions at storable.com .

sections.title: The role
paras: Storable brings together many products, built at different times on different systems. Operators, partners and AI agents need to work with all of them as one platform, and every call can reach tenant records, payments and facility access. You'll own how everyone builds on Storable, end to end: one consistent set of APIs across our products, a secure MCP server that lets AI agents act on Storable safely, and the standards underneath that keep every interface consistent and reliable.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Own the API layer that makes Storable's products work as one platform: one consistent way to reach tenants, units, leases and payments, whichever product they live in.
Define the shared resource model behind it with engineering and product teams: common entities, IDs and behavior across products.

Own Storable's MCP server and make it secure from day one: authenticated access, scoped permissions, tenant isolation, audit trails and protection against misuse, on the same identity and business logic as our APIs.

Set the standards every Storable interface follows: authentication and permissions, errors, versioning, pagination, rate limits, documentation and deprecation. Product teams, including Data & Analytics and AI Agents, decide what their APIs return and what their agents do. You own how every interface behaves.
Decide which products and capabilities come onto the platform first, based on what operators, partners and our own agents need most.
Make it work for everyone who builds on Storable, from a single operator's script to large portfolios and partners, with the right scopes and limits at each level.
Measure what matters: coverage across products, reliability, latency, security incidents and time to a first working integration.

sections.title: What you bring
bullets: Experience as a technical product manager owning APIs, a developer platform or integration products end to end: the interfaces, the platform behind them and the developers who use them.
Experience putting one consistent API over multiple products or backend systems: shared resource models, consistent IDs, and keeping data and behavior consistent across sources.

Strong understanding of how APIs work at scale: REST and event-driven design, idempotency, pagination, rate limiting and backward compatibility, and what each choice costs in reliability, latency and developer effort. You can read an API spec and call endpoints yourself.
Deep knowledge of API security: OAuth and scoped permissions, tenant isolation, audit logging and least privilege.
Hands-on experience building with MCP or LLM tool calling, and a clear view of the risks specific to agents, such as prompt injection and over-permissioned tools.
A record of driving adoption of shared standards across teams you don't manage.
Excellent writing. Your product and technical documents are clear enough that teams can decide and build from them.
You prototype and test integrations yourself with modern tools, including AI.

greenhouse:thetradedesk:5275512007.summary:
The Trade Desk is a global technology company and the world’s leading independent platform for digital advertising, with over 3,000 employees across more than 30 offices. Our technology helps advertisers reach the right audiences across the open internet — from streaming TV and podcasts to mobile apps, news, and more.

Advertising powers the content people love. By making it more transparent, effective, and responsible, we help support trusted journalism, quality entertainment, and creators worldwide. The world’s brands and agencies rely on us to reach their customers and grow their businesses responsibly.

The scale of our platform brings unique technical challenges — from processing massive datasets in real time to building systems that operate reliably on a global scale. When you work here, your impact is worldwide. We welcome diverse perspectives, encourage curiosity, and build…

sections.title: Who We Are
paras: The Trade Desk has also built something beyond our technology: a culture grounded in trust, ownership, and the belief that ambitious, principled people can change an industry. We value intellectual honesty, diverse perspectives, and teams that push each other to do better work. We celebrate big bets, learn from failures, and care deeply about getting things right — for our customers and for each other. If that resonates with you, we'd love to talk.

sections.title: Who We’re Looking For
paras: Data is foundational to The Trade Desk: how our products work, how our customers understand their investments, and how we build what comes next. We’re looking for a Staff Product Manager to shape the data platform that makes that possible. This is an opportunity to influence the foundations behind a global advertising business, building capabilities that help teams across the company move faster, make better decisions, and deliver more value to customers.

The scale makes this work especially compelling. Across channels and markets, our products depend on large volumes of data being collected, processed, and made available accurately, reliably, and efficiently. The decisions we make about those foundations shape what other teams can build, how quickly they can build it, and how well it performs. You’ll help ensure our data platform stays ahead of the business’s needs as our products, customers, and ambitions evolve. AI and agents are also expanding who uses data and what they can do with it. As software increasingly discovers, interprets, and acts on data, our platform must serve new kinds of users and make new workflows possible. You’ll help shape that evolution: building trusted, discoverable, and securely accessible data capabilities that enable teams to create AI-native products and agent-driven experiences.

We’re looking for someone who combines technical depth with the ability to make a complex vision clear and compelling. You’re curious about where the business is going, comfortable working with senior leaders across functions, and skilled at finding the shared needs behind different roadmaps. You love building alongside engineers, care about the people who depend on your platform, and can turn a long-term vision into practical investments that deliver value along the way.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
paras: As a Staff Product Manager, you will lead product vision, strategy, and priorities for the data platform, working closely with engineering and the teams that depend on it. This is a senior individual contributor role with influence across the organization. Your work will connect business direction to platform capabilities, helping teams meet today’s commitments while building the foundations for the next several years.
bullets: Set the vision and strategy for the data platform. Develop a clear point of view on how the platform needs to evolve and the opportunities it should enable. Translate that vision into a multi-year strategy and an actionable roadmap, with explicit priorities, tradeoffs, and measures of success.

Turn needs across teams into shared capabilities. Spend time with the engineers, data scientists, analysts, and product teams who produce and consume data. Understand their workflows and constraints, distinguish common problems from specialized needs, and prioritize investments that create value across the platform.

Build the plan with engineering. Partner closely with engineering leaders on how data is ingested, processed, stored, discovered, and served. Write clear product vision and requirements documents, evaluate options together, and make informed tradeoffs across performance, reliability, flexibility, cost, and time to value.

Make trusted data easier to use. Partner with engineering and relevant governance and security teams to establish expectations for data quality, freshness, discoverability, access, and reliability. Advocate for clear interfaces, documentation, and self-service workflows that make the platform easier to adopt and build on.

Deliver value throughout the journey. Break long-term investments into useful increments and coordinate dependencies, migrations, and adoption across teams. Balance new capabilities with improvements to existing foundations, keeping the roadmap responsive as business needs and technical understanding evolve.

sections.title: What You Bring to the Table
bullets: 6+ years of product management experience, including substantial experience building data platforms, infrastructure, or technical products at scale. You have led initiatives spanning multiple teams and carried them from strategy through delivery and adoption.

Experience setting a platform vision and strategy. You have translated needs across products or business areas into a coherent roadmap for shared capabilities. You can connect near-term decisions to a longer-term direction, distinguish durable needs from uncertain possibilities, and explain what to invest in now and what can wait.

Hands-on fluency with data. You’re strong in SQL and comfortable exploring datasets, investigating quality issues, and using evidence to test assumptions. You understand how data definitions, granularity, lineage, and freshness affect the products and decisions built on top of them.

A product mindset for internal platforms. You treat the teams using your platform as customers. You invest in understanding their work, care about developer experience and adoption, and recognize that a capability creates value when people can successfully use it.

Strong judgment and independent execution. You bring structure to ambiguous problems, prioritize across competing needs, and work closely with engineering to deliver useful increments. You take responsibility for results and keep improving the product after launch.

At Trella Health, our mission is simple: empowering meaningful change in healthcare.

We are building AI-enabled intelligence and workflows that help healthcare organizations make smarter decisions, strengthen operations, and support healthier outcomes for patients. Our platform connects health systems and post-acute providers through actionable intelligence and connected workflows that improve how care is coordinated across the healthcare continuum.

That work starts with our people. Trellavators are collaborative, curious, and committed to doing meaningful work that makes a measurable impact. We move quickly, support each other, keep our commitments, and continuously look for better ways to serve our customers and one another.

sections.title: Position Overview:
paras: We are looking for a Product Manager to join our Product team to own and grow a data domain spanning the full post-acute and value-based care continuum. You, as the Product Manager, will play a critical role in turning complex clinical and claims data into insights that help providers improve transitions of care, reduce readmissions, and deliver better outcomes across settings. You'll partner closely with data science, engineering, and GTM teams to ship AI-powered analytics that give post-acute providers and value-based organizations a clearer view of performance, referral patterns, and network leakage. This is a high-impact opportunity for someone who wants to shape how AI and clinical data come together to solve real problems in post-acute and value-based care, at a company positioned at the center of that shift.

sections.title: As a Product Manager at Trella, you will:
bullets: Own product strategy, roadmap, and execution for a clinical data domain spanning the full care continuum
Lead end-to-end product development, from discovery through delivery, across cross-functional teams including data science, data engineering, and software engineering
Translate clinical and claims data into actionable analytics, including transitions of care analysis, patient outcomes, performance benchmarking, referral patterns, cost, and network leakage

Identify and integrate AI/ML-driven capabilities (e.g., predictive analytics, risk stratification, anomaly detection) to enhance clinical insights and drive smarter decision-making for value-based care and post-acute providers

Build and ship AI-powered product features, from concept through adoption, including generative AI, predictive models, and intelligent automation embedded directly into clinical and operational workflows for users
Use AI tools daily across the full product lifecycle, including discovery, prototyping, requirements definition, stakeholder communication, and GTM enablement
Drive measurable business outcomes including ARR growth, customer retention, and NPS, ensuring product investments deliver impact
Own the clinical narrative around care transitions, including discharge planning, referral patterns, and cross-setting patient flow, translating those workflows into product requirements

sections.title: This job might be a fit for you if you have:
bullets: 4+ years of product management experience in B2B SaaS, with direct ownership of roadmap and product outcomes

Xealth sits at a unique intersection of healthcare data: we have deep integration with Electronic Health Records (EHRs), access to patient-generated data from third-party apps, and rich engagement data from patient clicks and actions. Integrating consumer wearable data and the power of AI will take us to new capabilities to care for people.

In this role, you will be the product visionary for how we use this data and leverage generative AI to drive meaningful actions. You will oversee our integration of wearable data both consumer facing and health system facing. Your mission is to bring next-generation AI capabilities to market that personalize and enhance these interactions for both patients and providers.

sections.title: What You'll Own and Deliver
bullets: Vision & Strategy: Own the roadmap for Xealth’s wearable solutions - transitioning from dashboards to AI-enabled insights and real time, data-driven interaction models.

Customer Focused: You will work with our customer teams as well as external health system relationships that you either bring or develop. Clinical insights are key to success and you will be expected to continuously seek out external validation of our product development priorities.
Data-Driven Iteration: Use, and advocate for, data to measure impact and iteratively improve the effectiveness of our tools.
Stakeholder Collaboration: Work with internal teams (engineering, customer success, partnerships) and external health system customers to launch and scale engagement tools.
Mission Focus: Make a real, positive difference in other people’s lives by finding new and compelling ways to support patients and clinicians.

sections.title: The Expertise You'll Bring
bullets: Experience: 5-10+ years of experience in Product Management for web-based, SaaS, or healthcare technology offerings.
Domain Expertise: Firm grasp on wearable technology including sensors, overall landscape, and their impact on wellness and healthcare.
Generative AI Expertise: Conversant with generative AI technology such as prompt engineering and MCP; able to drive product development of gen-AI product capabilities and offerings.
Technical Proficiency: Ability to meaningfully engage in design discussions with software developers and translate these into technical specifications.
Agile Leadership: Extensive experience in Lean, Agile, or Scrum software development processes.
Influencing Skills: Success as a cross-team influencer with a track record of managing expectations with both internal stakeholders and external enterprise customers.

paras: We are looking for a Senior Professional Services Consultant – Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) to join our Professional Services team. As organizations navigate AI-accelerated threats, cloud-first transformation, and sprawling multi-cloud data estates, you will turn complexity into clarity. You will architect, deploy, and optimize DSPM solutions alongside the broader Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform—driving expanded cloud-estate visibility, accurate sensitive-data inventory, reduced identity and credential exposure, and AI governance. Beyond traditional consulting, this role requires strong hands-on technical depth: you will configure complex data connectors, customize data classification pipelines, resolve production-level identity and integration challenges, and bridge real-world customer deployments directly with Core Engineering and Product Management.

Lead High-Touch Executive & Technical Engagements: Conduct strategic workshops, technical discoveries, and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), translating complex technical findings into actionable, executive-grade risk summaries and security roadmaps.

Execute Hands-On Data, Identity, & Workflow Engineering: Configure data connectors across major public clouds and data platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery), manage enterprise identity/IAM permissions, and build downstream SIEM/ticketing integrations.

Unblock Deployments & Shape Product Roadmap: Partner with Core Engineering to resolve complex production escalations, support pre-sales/POV engagements, and translate customer feedback into prioritized platform improvements.

lever:xsolla:50968b51-3346-412d-b7f7-987.summary:
You are a technical product manager who owns what a model optimises for, not just the roadmap around it. You have real depth in recommendation and ranking systems, and you will own the recommendation engine behind the Xsolla Advertising Products: the ranking that decides which offers millions of players see, and in what order.

You hold the bar high for how decisions get made. You can read a readout and say plainly what it does and does not support. You connect model performance to revenue without overclaiming, and you bring a low-ego, people-first approach to work that spans ML, analytics, ads operations, and commercial teams.

sections.title: ABOUT YOU
paras: If you are excited about using ML to build building the next generation of advertising, rewards and loyalty programs for mobile apps and games we want to hear from you.

sections.title: Responsibilities:
bullets: Own the recommendation engine as a product: ranking, relevance, and the model roadmap. Ranking quality is the product.
Set the objective the ranker optimises for, the constraints it works inside, and the guardrails and kill conditions that bound it. The target is eCPM today; what comes next is your call.

Own the metric definitions the whole team measures against, and settle the definitional questions that change the answer: gross against publisher-side RPU, app-load against impression-user denominators, mean of daily values against window totals.

Collaborate with on ML frameworks, experiment design, hold-outs, including pre-registered decision rules, power calculations, sample-ratio-mismatch checks, A/A validation, multiplicity correction, and named rollback triggers.
Collaborate with DS on readouts to evaluate model performace and readouts to business stakeholders readout: what the model did, what it cost, and what happens next.
Contribute the ranking perspective to the wider ads roadmap, including the seams where pricing, identity, and event telemetry meet ranking.

sections.title: Qualifications & Skills:
bullets: 6+ years in product management, with 3+ years owning a recommendation, ranking, personalization, or relevance system in production.

Deep understanding of experiment design and inference, including minimum detectable effect, statistical power, sample ratio mismatch, A/A testing, multiple-comparison correction, and pre-registration. You can tell when a readout will not support the claim being made from it, and you say so.

Working knowledge of the modelling itself: classification and regression, probability calibration, predicted conversion rate, expected-value objectives, and how the choice of objective changes model behavior.
Hands-on experience with ML and data platforms such as Snowflake, BigQuery, Spark, Airflow, dbt, MLFlow, Vertex AI, and feature stores.
Proven record of moving model changes into production traffic through a controlled experiment process, rather than shipping on a dashboard reading.
Knowledge of performance advertising economics and ad tech ecosystems, including eCPM, RPU, bid multipliers, campaign hierarchies, and attribution models.
SQL you write yourself, and enough comfort reading application code to verify a claim instead of taking it on trust.

Excellent written communication and stakeholder management across technical and non-technical audiences. Specs, decision records, and readouts are the output of this role, and other teams act on them without you in the room.
